quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The sentence starts with a negative subject. What follows from it?
quests.explanation: You heard exactly what was written. "Nobody" is negative by itself, so the verb that follows is positive: "told", not "didn't tell".
quests.prompt: Nobody told me the meeting was moved, so I went at the old time.
quests.sampleAnswer: Nobody told me the meeting was moved, so I went at the old time.
quests.followUpQuestion: Retell this in your own words, starting with "I went at the old time because..."

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: One pronoun at the end refers back to the people at the start.
quests.explanation: Them covers Sam and his sister, but him is only Sam. The sister would never receive the message.
quests.prompt: Sam and his sister were both away, so I left a message for them.
quests.sampleAnswer: Sam and his sister were both away, so I left a message for him.
quests.followUpQuestion: Who was the message for? Answer in a full sentence.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two pairs of shoes are compared using words for near and far.
quests.explanation: This and these point to things nearby, and that and those to things farther away. Swapping them swaps which pair fits.
quests.prompt: Those shoes are too small for me, but these ones fit perfectly.
quests.sampleAnswer: These shoes are too small for me, but those ones fit perfectly.
quests.followUpQuestion: Compare the two pairs of shoes in one sentence.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: One person is left out of a group. Who?
quests.explanation: The two versions are the same. "Everyone ... except" names the single exception at the end.
quests.prompt: Everyone in the office has signed the card except for the new intern.
quests.sampleAnswer: Everyone in the office has signed the card except for the new intern.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say who didn't sign the card, then explain why that might be.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The end of the sentence has a possessive pronoun. Whose car is being repaired?
quests.explanation: Hers means the sister's car and mine means the speaker's. That is the whole reason the sister lent her car.
quests.prompt: My sister lent me her car because hers was in the garage.
quests.sampleAnswer: My sister lent me her car because mine was in the garage.
quests.followUpQuestion: Whose car was in the garage? Say it clearly, using a possessive word.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The speaker gives an option and then compares. Which pronoun is used?
quests.explanation: "Either one" means it doesn't matter which, and "this one" points to the exit that is close.
quests.prompt: There are two exits. You can use either one, but this one is closer.
quests.sampleAnswer: There are two exits. You can use either one, but this one is closer.
quests.followUpQuestion: Recommend one exit to a visitor and give a reason.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The pronoun at the end refers back to someone unknown.
quests.explanation: Him assumes the caller is a man, while them keeps the caller unknown. Native speakers usually say them when the person isn't known.
quests.prompt: If someone calls while I'm out, could you ask him to leave a number?
quests.sampleAnswer: If someone calls while I'm out, could you ask them to leave a number?
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you would ask a colleague to do if someone calls for you.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Notice who is being invited: how many people, and whose office.
quests.explanation: "The two of us" is a natural way to say "both of us".
quests.prompt: The manager wants to see the two of us in her office after lunch.
quests.sampleAnswer: The manager wants to see the two of us in her office after lunch.
quests.followUpQuestion: Reply to the manager as if you were one of the two people.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: This includes a decision and a question to a friend.
quests.explanation: Nothing was altered in this one. "Either of them" means one or the other, and it is followed by a plural pronoun.
quests.prompt: I can't decide between these two jackets. Do you like either of them?
quests.sampleAnswer: I can't decide between these two jackets. Do you like either of them?
quests.followUpQuestion: Answer the question: which of the two would you choose, and why?

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Who is being picked up? Focus on the pronoun after "pick".
quests.explanation: Us includes the speaker and you doesn't. If the speaker isn't being picked up, the story doesn't make sense.
quests.prompt: They said they'd pick you up at the airport, but we haven't seen them.
quests.sampleAnswer: They said they'd pick us up at the airport, but we haven't seen them.
quests.followUpQuestion: Explain in one sentence what went wrong with the pick-up.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two sentences, one question and one explanation.
quests.explanation: They are identical. "Someone" and "nobody" refer to unknown people, and both take a singular verb.
quests.prompt: Whose bag is this? Someone left it on the train, and nobody has claimed it.
quests.sampleAnswer: Whose bag is this? Someone left it on the train, and nobody has claimed it.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what happened to the bag, using someone and nobody.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A possessive word before "new flat" tells you who lives there.
quests.explanation: Our means the speaker's home, and your means the listener's. They would visit a different address.
quests.prompt: My parents are coming next month, and I'd like them to see our new flat.
quests.sampleAnswer: My parents are coming next month, and I'd like them to see your new flat.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you would show your visitors first in your own home.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A request that uses "that" and "the one". What is being pointed to?
quests.explanation: "The one next to the printer" identifies the folder among others.
quests.prompt: Could you pass me that folder on the desk, the one next to the printer?
quests.sampleAnswer: Could you pass me that folder on the desk, the one next to the printer?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask for something on a desk, describing it so the listener knows which one.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: There's a lot of "their" and "they" in this sentence. Follow who owns what.
quests.explanation: "Theirs" replaces "their dog" and shows that the neighbours deny owning it.
quests.prompt: We asked our neighbours to keep their dog quiet, but they said it wasn't theirs.
quests.sampleAnswer: We asked our neighbours to keep their dog quiet, but they said it wasn't theirs.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what the neighbours claimed, in your own words.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A phone call is promised. Whom will she call?
quests.explanation: Him is a man the speaker has not named, and her is the sister who was just mentioned. The promise is about a different person's phone call.
quests.prompt: She told her sister that she would call him back after the meeting.
quests.sampleAnswer: She told her sister that she would call her back after the meeting.
quests.followUpQuestion: Explain who will call whom, so there is no confusion.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The sentence opens with a negative subject that takes a singular verb.
quests.explanation: The recording follows the text word for word. "Neither of" is followed by a plural noun, but the verb "likes" is singular in careful English.
quests.prompt: Neither of my roommates likes cooking, so we usually order takeaway.
quests.sampleAnswer: Neither of my roommates likes cooking, so we usually order takeaway.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what none of your friends or family enjoys doing, using neither or none.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A group is divided in two parts. How big is the first part?
quests.explanation: Most means the majority, and some is just a few. A teacher planning the next task would react differently.
quests.prompt: Most of the students finished early, but the others needed more time.
quests.sampleAnswer: Some of the students finished early, but the others needed more time.
quests.followUpQuestion: Describe how a group finished a task, using most and others.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A demonstrative word before "party" shows where the speaker is.
quests.explanation: This party means the one the speaker is at, and that party means one somewhere else. You hear whether they are there or not.
quests.prompt: I don't know anyone at that party except the host and his brother.
quests.sampleAnswer: I don't know anyone at this party except the host and his brother.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say who you would know at a party, and who you wouldn't.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A talk is required from each person. What will it be about?
quests.explanation: One version is about the firm and the other is about the speakers. A candidate would prepare completely different material.
quests.prompt: Each of the candidates has to give a short talk about the company.
quests.sampleAnswer: Each of the candidates has to give a short talk about themselves.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what each candidate has to do, in your own words.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A person is not identified. Which pronoun helps to refer back?
quests.explanation: "Which one" is used when choosing from a known group, such as your colleagues.
quests.prompt: I lent my umbrella to a colleague, but I can't remember which one.
quests.sampleAnswer: I lent my umbrella to a colleague, but I can't remember which one.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you can't remember, and ask the listener to help.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Responsibility is passed from the speaker to another group.
quests.explanation: "Theirs" is a possessive pronoun that stands for "their problem".
quests.prompt: It's not my problem, it's theirs, and they should be the ones to fix it.
quests.sampleAnswer: It's not my problem, it's theirs, and they should be the ones to fix it.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say whose responsibility this is, and what should happen next.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: There are two printers. Which is which?
quests.explanation: This is a straight match. "The other one" refers to the one that has not been mentioned yet.
quests.prompt: One of the printers is broken, but the other one works fine.
quests.sampleAnswer: One of the printers is broken, but the other one works fine.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say which of the two printers you would use, and why.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A question offers two alternatives. Listen to the second one.
quests.explanation: Going alone and going with friends are different answers. The second half of the question is the part the speaker really wants to know.
quests.prompt: Did you go to the concert with your sister, or did you go alone?
quests.sampleAnswer: Did you go to the concert with your sister, or did you go with friends?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask the same question about a different person.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: One detail identifies which car. It's a colour word at the end.
quests.explanation: Black and blue are easy to mix up in an announcement. Someone would walk to the wrong car.
quests.prompt: Somebody has left their lights on again, and I think it's the black car.
quests.sampleAnswer: Somebody has left their lights on again, and I think it's the blue car.
quests.followUpQuestion: Describe a car you saw, so others can identify it.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: An instruction includes an announcement to a group.
quests.explanation: "Everybody" behaves like a singular noun, but the meaning is plural.
quests.prompt: Please tell everybody that the class has moved to the room next door.
quests.sampleAnswer: Please tell everybody that the class has moved to the room next door.
quests.followUpQuestion: Pass the message on to a group, as if you were the teacher.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two people are invited, then one is left out. Follow the numbers.
quests.explanation: "Both of them" and "only one" contrast two with one.
quests.prompt: I wanted to invite both of them, but only one could come.
quests.sampleAnswer: I wanted to invite both of them, but only one could come.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say how many people were invited and how many came.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Someone is blamed. Is it the speaker's colleague or the man himself?
quests.explanation: Himself is a reflexive pronoun for the same person, while other people means someone else. They describe opposite characters.
quests.prompt: He always blames himself when something goes wrong at work.
quests.sampleAnswer: He always blames other people when something goes wrong at work.
quests.followUpQuestion: Describe how someone reacts to a mistake, in your own words.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The request ends with a possessive pronoun. Whose phone?
quests.explanation: His and yours are two people. Asking a stranger for their phone can lead to an awkward moment.
quests.prompt: My phone is almost dead, so could I borrow his for a minute?
quests.sampleAnswer: My phone is almost dead, so could I borrow yours for a minute?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask to borrow something, and make clear whose it is.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: This includes a negative subject and a pronoun that means the second person.
quests.explanation: Listening and reading agree here. "The other one" refers to the second person and "neither of us" means both are ignorant.
quests.prompt: Neither of us had any idea where the other one was parked.
quests.sampleAnswer: Neither of us had any idea where the other one was parked.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what the two of you don't know, using neither.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Blame moves from one person to another. Listen to who ends up responsible.
quests.explanation: Hers and his are both possessive pronouns, and mixing them up could put the blame on the wrong colleague.
quests.prompt: Everyone thought the mistake was mine, but it turned out to be hers.
quests.sampleAnswer: Everyone thought the mistake was mine, but it turned out to be his.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say who made the mistake and who was blamed, in your own words.
